description: Engine-backed golden cases at the statutory edges that Phases 1-5 step over: the SSS EC threshold and MSC cap, the PhilHealth premium floor, and the withholding-table bracket edges. Every expected value is hand-derived below from the published rules, never copied from engine output.

sources.sss: SSS Circular 2024-006 (effective 2025-01-01): employee 5% and employer 10% of the monthly salary credit (MSC); MSC floor 5,000, cap 35,000, step 500, so compensation from X250 to X749.99 maps to MSC X500/X000 (14,750 -> 15,000; 34,750 -> 35,000); EC is 10 per month when MSC < 15,000 and 30 from MSC 15,000.
sources.philHealth: PhilHealth 2024 schedule: 5% premium on a base of at least 10,000 and at most 100,000, shared equally between employee and employer.
sources.pagIbig: Pag-IBIG Fund (effective 2024-02): 2% employee and 2% employer of the fund salary, capped at a fund salary of 10,000.
sources.bir: BIR Revised Withholding Tax Tables effective 2023 onward, semi-monthly: taxable <= 10,417 exempt; 10,417-16,667 at 15% over 10,417; 16,667-33,333 at 937.50 + 20% over 16,667; 33,333-83,333 at 4,270.70 + 25% over 33,333. Taxable compensation = cutoff gross - employee SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG.

assumptions: Monthly-salaried employees, September 1-15 2026 cutoff, no attendance deductions, allowances, loans or leave. Statutory deduction timing is 'split', so each cutoff carries 50% of the monthly contribution (EC and employer shares likewise).
MSC is derived from the monthly salary as the full monthly compensation. The employee is 'Active' in NCR.

Salaries 9,000 and 14,740-14,760 are below the NCR minimum-wage equivalent. They are valid fictional part-time rates used to reach the SSS and PhilHealth edges, and the engine only flags them for review.
Withholding is rounded to the centavo. Salaries were chosen so no hand value sits on a half-centavo.

sssAtEcThreshold.description: Monthly 14,760, 20 pesos over 14,740 but across the 14,750 edge: MSC 15,000 (14,750-15,249.99). EE 750 -> 375.00; ER 1,500 -> 750.00; EC 30/month -> 15.00 (EC steps from 10 to 30 at MSC 15,000). PhilHealth 14,760 x 2.5% = 369 -> 184.50. Pag-IBIG 100. Gross 7,380. Taxable = 7,380 - 375 - 184.50 - 100 = 6,720.50. Net 6,720.50, which is LOWER than the 14,740 worker's 6,723.25 despite higher pay.

philHealthBelowFloor.description: Monthly 9,000: PhilHealth uses the 10,000 floor, not the salary: 5% x 10,000 = 500, employee half 250 -> 125.00 per cutoff (5% of 9,000 would be 112.50). SSS: MSC 9,000 (8,750-9,249.99), EE 450 -> 225.00, ER 900 -> 450.00, EC 10 -> 5.00. Pag-IBIG fund salary 9,000: 2% = 180 -> 90.00 each. Gross 4,500. Statutory 225 + 125 + 90 = 440. Taxable 4,060, no tax. Net 4,060.

taxInFifteenPercentBracket.description: Monthly 36,000: gross 18,000. SSS 875, PhilHealth 450, Pag-IBIG 100 -> taxable 16,575 (just under the 16,667 edge). Tax = (16,575 - 10,417) x 15% = 923.70. Deductions 1,425 + 923.70 = 2,348.70. Net 15,651.30.

taxJustPastTwentyFivePercentEdge.description: Monthly 70,400: gross 35,200. SSS 875, PhilHealth 880, Pag-IBIG 100 -> taxable 33,345 (12 past the 33,333 edge). Tax = 4,270.70 + (33,345 - 33,333) x 25% = 4,270.70 + 3.00 = 4,273.70. Deductions 1,855 + 4,273.70 = 6,128.70. Net 29,071.30. Higher pay than the 70,000 worker by 200, and only 156.60 more net.

limitations: Regular 13th-month pay is not computed by regular payroll runs (only final pay and year-end), so it is not covered by this phase.
The PhilHealth 100,000 ceiling and Pag-IBIG 10,000 cap are already exercised by Phase 2A (salaries of 100,000 and above and 10,000 and above).
Daily-paid and hourly workers' statutory contributions are not asserted.
Second-cutoff statutory true-up (month-to-date reconciliation) is covered by Phase 2B.
